name: Tucker Field
use: Turf field for UNH soccer and women's lacrosse, plus Oyster River Youth Association; planned future stadium
builtText: Phase I built during the 2018-19 academic year; lights switched on October 2, 2025

renovations.what: Field lighting funded by a $2 million gift from Greg and Corinna Tucker; lit at a ceremony October 2, 2025

facts.text: Phase I was completed in 2018-19; the field opened for training and hosted select women's lacrosse games in 2020.
UNH Athletics' Phase II plan called for lighting, a grandstand for about 2,000, a press box and covered team benches, estimated at $1.8 million.
Greg and Corinna Tucker gave $2 million for lights (announced 2024); the lights were switched on at halftime of a women's soccer game on October 2, 2025.
Home to UNH soccer and women's lacrosse and used by the Oyster River Youth Association; plans call for stadium seating, concessions, restrooms and a press box.

verdict: Soccer and lacrosse turf with new $2M lights; grandstand still only planned.
notes: The only licensed image is the 2025 Wildcat Stadium aerial; the lit turf soccer field in its upper left is identified as Tucker Field from its position (south-east of the stadium per notunh's gazetteer) and its new light poles. That identification is mine, not the uploader's; the judge should confirm. The field appears to be synthetic turf with lines for soccer; no buildings. Corrections to old row: Phase II estimate was $1.8M for about 2,000 seats (old row said ~$4M and 2,000-3,000 seats); "site of old Lewis Field" not confirmed. Same image file as wildcat-stadium/01.jpg, copied.
judgeNotes: Open-air field: unranked. Dropped 01.jpg: it is the Wildcat Stadium aerial with Tucker Field a corner of the frame, so it doesn't represent this field.
